rationale: The only directly matching evidence-supported pattern is P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure), which would change test_artifacts_subsystem from fail-fast: false to fail-fast: true. However, this job runs four test partitions on FPGA hardware (vck190-subsystem, 180-minute timeout each), and each partition executes a distinct nextest test subset (--partition count:N/4). Cancelling remaining partitions on failure would reduce test coverage visibility and failure diagnostics, which conflicts with the requirement to preserve intended build and test coverage. The pattern's contraindications ('Every matrix outcome is required', 'Full failure diagnostics are required') apply to test partitions, and there is no explicit study policy making remaining matrix results dispensable. Other patterns (caching, timeouts, Bazel parallelism) are either already present in the workflow or not applicable (no Bazel usage). No supported optimization preserves coverage while fitting this workflow.
